Vehicle 1 was traveling east in the eastbound lane of Sunray Drive approaching the intersection with the driveway to [ADDRESS] (Publix). Vehicle 2 was stopped in the southbound lane of the driveway to Publix at the intersection with Sunray Drive, waiting to turn right onto westbound Sunray Drive. Driver 1 took the left turn from Sunray Drive into the driveway of Publix too short and failed to observe Vehicle 2. The front left of Vehicle 1 collided with the front right of Vehicle 2. Driver 2 attempted to follow Vehicle 1 to get the tag but was only able to describe Vehicle 1 as a black 4 door car. Driver 2 called law enforcement and returned to the scene of the crash. There was vehicle debris observed in the intersection of the Publix driveway and Sunray Drive. With no other known information about Driver 1 or Vehicle 1 follow up cannot be conducted.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was traveling southbound on U.S. 19 (State Road 55), in the left turn lane, just north of Embassy Blvd. Vehicle 2 (V02) was traveling northbound on U.S. 19 (State Road 55), in the outside lane, just north of Embassy Blvd. Driver 1 attempted to make a left turn into a nearby plaza parking lot, but in doing so, failed to yield to oncoming V02. As a result, the front of V01 collided with the front left of V02's trailer. This collision directed V02 and its trailer eastward, and into a ditch on the shoulder of U.S. 19. The collision with the ditch cause disabling damage to the undercarriage (wheels) of V02. Concurrently, the right side of V02's trailer collided with a light pole belonging to FDOT, on the shoulder of U.S. 19. V01 came to final rest facing east, occupying the center and outside lane of U.S. 19. V02 and its trailer remained at final rest at the area of collision with the ditch and light pole.

V1 was traveling eastbound, on SR 60, approaching St. Cloud Av S in the right through lane. V2 was traveling southbound, on St. Cloud Av S, approaching SR 60. V2 was stopped at the red light. V2 received a green light, and continued southbound on St. Cloud Av S. V1 received a red light and failed to stop and yield the right of way to V2. The front left of V1 struck the front of V2. The driver of V1 (D1) advised she was traveling eastbound on SR 60, and turned to look at her child, who was in the back seat. When she turned back around, she noticed the light was red, but was unable to stop. D1 complained of injuries to her shoulder and back pain. All occupants were wearing their seat belts. D1 was given two citations. One was for running a red light and the second was for operating a vehicle with a learners permit with no licensed driver over [AGE]. The driver of V2 (D2) advised she was sitting at the red light waiting to cross the intersection. The light turned green and she proceeded through the intersection, when the other driver (D1), ran the red light and hit her. D2 complained of neck and chest pain. She was wearing her seat belt.

Vehicle 1 (V1) was southbound on Jordana Way approaching the stop sign at Sunray Drive. Vehicle 2 (V2) was eastbound on Sunray Drive approaching Jordana Way. V1 initiated a left turn onto eastbound Sunray Drive without stopping at the stop sign. The right front of V1 struck the left side of V2. According to Driver 2 (D2), after the collision, V1 continued east on Sunray Drive without acknowledging a crash occurred. When speaking with Driver 1 (D1), she was unsure of the events of the crash and stated "It just happened so fast, I hardly drive. I was just going to vote". Both vehicles were removed from the roadway prior to my arrival and relocated to the Aldi's parking lot at the southeast corner of the intersection of US Highway 19 and Sunray Drive.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was stopped facing west on the private driveway located at [ADDRESS] at the intersection for Mariner Boulevard. Vehicle 2 (V02) was traveling south in the outside lane on Mariner Boulevard, approaching V01. Driver 1 (D01) failed to observe V02 approaching and attempted to make a left turn onto Mariner Boulevard. Subsequently, the front right of V01 collided with the left side of V02. Both vehicles came to final rest near the area of collision and were moved prior to my arrival.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was traveling south on Collier Parkway, in the left turn lane, south of State Road 54. Vehicle 2 (V02) was traveling north on Collier Parkway, in the outside lane, south of State Road 54. Vehicle 3 (V03) was stopped, westbound in the parking lot access of Willow Bend Towne Centre plaza parking lot access, in the left turn lane, south of State Road 54. Driver 1 attempted to make a left turn into the plaza parking lot access, but in doing so, failed to yield the right of way to Driver 2. As a result, the front of V02 collided with the right side of V01. V01 was directed towards V03, colliding with its front right. All three vehicles were relocated to the plaza parking lot, prior to my arrival. Note: Both Driver 1 and Driver 2 stated that traffic in the inside and center northbound travel lanes of Collier Parkway was stopped.

Vehicle 1 (V-1) was traveling southbound on Collier Parkway south of SR 54 and came to a stop in the median left turn lane to turn into the driveway access for the parking lot of the [NAME] Family Church. Vehicle 2 (V-2) was traveling northbound on Collier Parkway in the right lane approaching the driveway access for the [NAME] Family Church. Traffic in the right and center lanes of northbound Collier Parkway were stopped and backed up with heavy traffic, due to the intersection of SR 54. Driver 1 stated the stopped traffic in the northbound lanes left her room to turn and she thought the right lane was free of traffic, so she accelerated making a left turn into the path of V-2. This caused the front of V-2 to strike the right front of V-1. Both vehicles were moved into the parking lot prior to my arrival. Driver 2 stated traffic in the left and center lanes for northbound Collier Parkway were stopped, but there were no vehicles ahead of him in the right lane. As he approached the driveway access, V-1 suddenly turned in front of him and he could not avoid a collision. There were no injuries reported. Both vehicles were towed from the scene due to the damages.

V1 was traveling east on E Brandon Blvd approaching the intersection of N Parsons Ave. V1 ran the steady red light at the intersection and struck the driver side of V2. V2 was pulling a utility trailer, which swung around and struck V1. V2 was stopped for traffic at the intersection of N Parsons Ave and E Brandon Blvd. The light turned green and V2 proceeded through the intersection. V2 was suddenly struck on the driver side by the front of V1. D1 stated he was traveling East on Brandon Blvd approaching the intersection of N Parsons Ave. D1 said he could not see the light at the intersection due to the sun being in his eyes. He judged the light by watching the vehicle next to him. He saw the vehicle next to him speed up, so he figured the light was green. It was not until he saw V2 entering the intersection that he realized the light must have been red. D1 reported minor leg pain and was transported to Brandon Hospital by HCFR. D2 stated he was stopped for traffic at the intersection of N Parsons Ave and E Brandon Blvd. The light turned green and he proceeded through the intersection. V2 was suddenly struck on the driver side by the front of V1. D2 stated he heard a horn honking prior to the collision and believed it came from V1. D2 reported no injuries. It should be noted according to online resources, the sun's azimuth was at a 16 degree altitude in the eastern sky at [TIME] on today's date in Brandon, FL.

V01 was traveling eastbound on CR-52, approaching the intersection of US-19 in the left turn lane. V02 was traveling southbound on US-19, approaching the intersection of SR-52 in the left turn lane. Driver -2 stated that she had a solid green arrow and began to negotiate a left turn onto SR-52 when the passenger side of V02 was struck. Driver 2 stated she watched V01 flee the scene northbound on US-19 but was unsure of make or model. V02 was moved into a near by parking lot prior to Troopers arrival.

Vehicle-1 (V01) was traveling north in the inside lane on US-19 (Commercial Way) approaching Osowaw Blvd. Vehicle-2 (V02) was traveling east in the outside lane on Osowaw Blvd approaching US-19 (Commercial Way). Driver-1 did not stop V01 for the red traffic signal. The front right of V02 struck the left side of V01. Prior to Trooper arrival both vehicles were moved from area of collision to the center median of Spring Hill Dr. Witness stated that he was behind V01 and it did not stop for the red traffic signal.

Vehicle 1 was westbound on CR-574 (Spring Hill Drive) stopped observing a flashing red traffic control signal. Vehicle 2 was southbound in the inside lane on US-19 (Commercial Way) approaching a flashing yellow traffic control signal. Driver 1 stated that he came to a complete stop, and then proceeded to continue west, entering the intersection. Driver 1 stated that prior to entering the intersection he did not observe Vehicle 2 approaching. Driver 2 stated that he remembered facing a flashing yellow light as he entered the intersection at which time Vehicle 1 crossed into his path of travel. Driver 1 proceeded into the intersection failing to observe the approaching southbound Vehicle 2. As a result, the front of Vehicle 2 collided with the right front side of Vehicle 1. Due to the initial collision, the rear of Vehicle 2 wrap/rotated clockwise resulting in the left side of Vehicle 2 impacting the right side of Vehicle 1. Vehicle 1 veered southwest impacting a "No U-Turn" sign in the raised curb median of Osowaw Blvd. Vehicle 1 came to final rest facing west straddling the raised curb median. Vehicle 2 rolled forward coming to final rest west of the area of collision.

Vehicle-1 (V01) was westbound in the inside left turn lane of State Road 50 approaching a steady red arrow signal at the intersection of Mariner Boulevard. Vehicle-2 (V02) was eastbound in the center lane of State Road 50 approaching a steady green traffic signal at the intersection of Mariner Boulevard. Driver-1 (D01) failed to stop for the red light and attempted to make a left turn onto Mariner Boulevard. V01 entered into the direct path of V02. As a result, the front of V02 struck the right rear side of V01. Prior to my arrival, both vehicles relocated from the area of collision. Witness-1 (W01) stated that she was traveling in the outside eastbound lane of State Road 50 and was behind V02. She stated that their traffic light was green. D01 was cited for failure to stop at a red light.

Vehicle-1 (V-1) was in the center median intersection along southbound Collier Parkway just south of SR-54. Vehicle-2 (V-2) was in the outside right turn lane traveling on northbound Collier Parkway approaching SR-54. Driver of V-1 failed to yield the right of way to approaching opposite direction traffic while attempting a left turn into a Church access drive causing the front right of V-1 to collide with the front left of V-2. V-1 and V-2 moved from final rest to a nearby lot located along the northbound side of Collier Parkway just south of SR-54 prior to arrival.

V1 was stopped in a private driveway, off of Parsons Ave, just north of E Brandon Blvd, attempting to cross traffic by making a left turn. V2 was stopped in traffic within the inside lane of southbound traffic. V1 was operated in a careless manner, and the rear driver tire area of V1 struck the rear passenger bumper of V2 as V1 was attempting to make a left turn. Neither driver complained of injury, and neither vehicle required a tow.

Driver 1 (D01) of Vehicle 1 (V01) advised he was traveling east on State Road 54 in the center lane just west Village Lakes Shopping Center Drive. Vehicle 2 (V02) was stopped facing west in the westbound left turn lane of State Road 54 just east of Village Lakes Shopping Center Drive. D01 advised he entered the intersection at a solid green light as V02 began to make a left turn entering the path of V01 resulting in the front left side of V01 striking the front end of V02. Driver 2 (D02) of V02 advised he was stopped facing west in the westbound left turn lane of State Road 54 just east of Village Lakes Shopping Center Drive. V01 was traveling east on State Road 54 in the center lane just west Village Lakes Shopping Center Drive. D02 advised he entered the intersection at a solid green left turn arrow. D02 advised V01 then entered the intersection resulting in the front left side of V01 striking the front end of V02. I spoke with a witness who saw the crash but was unable to advise who had a green light/the right-of-way. Due to the impact V01 continued to travel east while rotating counterclockwise. While rotating V01 began to veer northeast entering the median before coming to final rest facing north in the median of State Road 54 just east of Village Lakes Shopping Center Drive. Due to the impact V02 rotated counterclockwise coming to final rest facing south in the intersection of State Road 54 and Village Lakes Shopping Center Drive. Due to conflicing statements neither drivers were cited.

V01 was traveling south in the inside lane of southbound US-19 (SR-55), approaching the intersection of SR-52. V02 was negotiating a left turn in the outside left turn lane of westbound SR-52, to southbound US-19. V03 was negotiating a left turn in the inside left turn lane of westbound SR-52, to southbound US-19. V04 was stopped at the red traffic signal in the inside left turn lane of northbound US-19, at the intersection of SR-52. V02 and V03 proceeded to make the left turn with a steady left arrow traffic signal. Driver-1 failed to observe the steady red traffic signal. As a result, V01 traveled through into the intersection into the paths of V02 and V03. The left side of V01 collided with the front right of V02, and the front right of V03. V01 continued in a southeast direction and rotated into the path of V04. The rear left corner of V01 collided with the left side of V04. V01 came to final rest in the left turn lane of northbound US-19. Prior to my arrival, V02, V03, and V04 were moved to the shoulder of southbound US-19, south of SR-52. Driver-1 was inattentive at the time of collision. Driver-1 mentioned she was reaching for a vape and she was also unsure of the traffic light signal. The listed witnesses and other involved drivers confirmed V01 ran a red traffic signal.

V01 was stopped at the stop sign in the northbound lane of Aloha Place, intersecting with Sunray Drive V02 was traveling westbound on Sunray Drive, approaching the intersection of Aloha Place. Based on Statements from Driver-1, she looked east and west for oncoming traffic as she was stopped at the stop sign. Driver-1 stated that she did not see any oncoming traffic, so she departed from the stop bar. V01 crossed the eastbound lane and entered the westbound lane. As V01 entered the westbound lane, V02 was occupying the westbound lane. The front of V01 collided with the left side of V02. V02 then turned 180 degrees from the impact, leaving V02 facing eastbound in the eastbound lane. Driver-2's statements of the event corroborated Driver-1's statements. Contributing Cause: Driver-1 failed to yield to oncoming traffic, resulting in a crash. No citation was issued due to statements about V02's headlights being on when the Trooper had not inquired about them being on at the time of the crash. Trooper felt that V02's headlights might not have been on at the time of the crash but had no proof other than the need to reassure Trooper that they were on.

Vehicle 2 was traveling north on Mariner Blvd passed Cortez Blvd when vehicle 1 pulled out of the circle k parking lot the west side exit to travel south on Mariner Blvd. Driver of vehicle 1 stated he looked before he exited the parking lot but he did not see vehicle 2. No injuries were reported.

V01 was traveling westbound in the left turn on Darlington Road, approaching U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55). NM01 was traveling westbound in the marked crosswalk on U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55), at the intersection of Darlington Road. As NM01 was by median of U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55), V01 attempted to make a left onto U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55). The left side (left side view mirror) of V01 struck NM01. V01 relocated from the area of collision to the Dunkin Donuts parking lot located at [ADDRESS], prior to my arrival. NM01 was transported to Advent Health North Pinellas, prior to my arrival. Upon my arrival, V01 remained where it was relocated to. Witness stated he was stopped in the eastbound left turn on Darlington Road at the intersection of U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55). Witness stated the traffic lights for eastbound traffic on Darlington Road were red and traffic in the westbound lanes of Darlington Road had the green light and were going. Witness stated he saw V01 strike NM01 and went to help NM01. Witness stated NM01 had the crosswalk signal and had around 35 seconds on the counter when he looked.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was westbound, in the outside left turn lane, on County Road 574 (Spring Hill Drive), approaching a steady red traffic signal at the intersection of U.S. Highway 19 (Commercial Way). Vehicle 2 (V02) was northbound, in the center lane, on U.S. Highway 19, approaching a steady green traffic signal at the intersection of County Road 574. V01 slowed and stopped at the steady red traffic signal. Driver-1 accelerated into the into the intersection while still having a steady red traffic signal. Driver-2 braked and attempted to swerve left to avoid a collision, however; a collision was unavoidable at which time the front of V01 collided with the right side of V02. As a result of the collision, V01 rotated clockwise, coming to final rest within the intersection, facing northeast. V02 rotated counterclockwise and traveled northwest before coming to final rest in the southbound travel lanes of U.S. Highway 19. Upon interviewing Driver-1, she stated she was stopped at the steady red light then realized her vehicle was rolling forward. Driver-1 stated her husband began yelling to her to "stop" and upon attempting to depress the brake pedal, Driver-1 advertently depressed the accelerator pedal. This action caused V01 to accelerate into the intersection and the collision to occur. All witnesses attached to this report advised V01 was stopped at the steady red traffic signal then accelerated into the intersection, colliding with V02. Note: Driver-1 was wearing blue none laces shoes and had deep grip and grooves. The passenger of V02 was listed as a Trauma Alert and transported to a Trauma Center as a result of the collision.

V01 was eastbound in the left turn lane of State Road 60, approaching the driveway of [ADDRESS] V02 was westbound, in the outside center westbound lane of State Road 60, approaching the driveway of [ADDRESS] V03 was stopped facing south on the driveway of [ADDRESS], north of State Road 60. D01 began to turn left toward the driveway and V01 entered the path of V02. The front of V02 struck the front right of V01. V02 was redirected toward V03, and the front of V02 struck the front left of V03. V01 was redirected to the west, then driven to a controlled stop in the bicycle lane west of the area of collision. V02 and V03 came to final rest at the second area of collision.

Vehicle 1 was southbound on US 19 in the left turn bay. Vehicle 2 was northbound on US 19 in the right turn lane. Vehicle 1 proceeded to cross the northbound lane, entering the path of Vehicle 2. The front of Vehicle 2 stuck the right front side of Vehicle 1. Prior to my arrival both vehicles were moved from the area of collision.

Driver 2 of Vehicle 2 advised she was traveling northbound on Commercial Way approaching the Toucan Trail intersection. Driver 2 said her light was green and she observed a white car (Vehicle 1) to be turning from the southbound side of Commercial Way onto Toucan Trail. Driver 2 said Vehicle 1 turned into her path so she swerved to miss the vehicle but was struck on the driver side rear quarter panel which caused her vehicle to spin. Driver 2 said she then pulled to the side of the roadway and awaited law enforcement. Driver 2 said she was not injured and did remove her vehicle from the scene. Contact was made with Witness 1 who advised he was sitting in the turn lane on Toucan Trail to turn onto Commercial Way southbound. Witness 1 said Vehicle 2 had a steady green light and Vehicle 1 had a flashing yellow light. Vehicle 1 then turned into the path of Vehicle 2 and crashed into the rear of Vehicle 2. Driver 1 of Vehicle 1 advised he was traveling southbound on Commercial Way and was going to turn onto Toucan Trail. Driver 1 said as he was turning he did not see Vehicle 2 because it's headlights were not on. Driver 1 said he did not see the car until it was too late and they crashed. Driver 1 said he was not injured and did remove his vehicle from the scene. Contact was again made with Witness 1 who advised Vehicle 2 had its headlights on. Driver 1 was cited for failure to yield right of way approaching or entering an intersection.

V-1 VEHICLE WAS AT THE RED LIGHT WANTING TO TURN L ON FRONTAGE RD, V-2 WAS HEADING NORTH ON MARINER BLVD, V-1 TURNED IN FRONT OF V-2 AT THE INTERSECTION, STRIKING THE FRONT OF V-2 AND V-1 REAR SECTION OF THE VEHICLE. V-1 HAD TO BE TOWED DUE TO THE DAMAGE. V-1 DRIVER WENT TO OAK HILL HOSPITAL FOR OBSERVATION.

Vehicle-1 was traveling north on US 19 (State Road 55) in the outside lane. Vehicle-2 was traveling west on CR 574 (Spring Hill Drive) in the inside left turn lane. Driver-1 stated that while traveling north on US 19, he did not notice that the signal was red and proceeded into the intersection, where he collided with a vehicle entering from Spring Hill Drive. Driver-2 stated that he was stopped at the red signal, and when it turned green, he proceeded into the intersection in order to travel south on US 19 when the collision occurred. The right front of vehicle-1 collided with the left front of vehicle-2. After the collision, both vehicles came to rest facing north parallel to each other in the northbound outside lane.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was northbound in the center lane of US Highway 19 approaching Sunray Drive. Vehicle 2 (V02) was westbound in left turn lane of Sunray Drive approaching US Highway 19. V02 had the green left turn arrow and proceeded into the intersection. V01 ran the red light. The front of V01 struck the left side of V02. V01 came to final rest facing east in the center of the intersection. V02 came to final rest facing northwest in the center of the intersection.

Vehicle 1 (V-1) was traveling eastbound on Sunray Drive approaching the intersection of US-19. Vehicle 2 (V-2) was traveling northbound on US-19 approaching the intersection of Sunray Drive in the inside lane. Both driver's claimed to have the green light. V-1 and V-2 made contact in the middle of the intersection. The front of V-2 struck the right side of V-1. V-2 came to final rest in the inside lane of US-19 facing north and V-1 relocated to a nearby parking lot. I attempted to contact the listed witness in order to determine who ran the red light. A voice-mail was left at [TIME] The witness never contacted FHP to provide a statement, therefore no citations were issued.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was southbound on US 19 approaching the intersection of Toucan Trail in the center lane at a steady green traffic light. Non Motorist 1 (NM01) was crossing US 19 from east to west and was approaching the southbound lanes of US 19 at a red pedestrian traffic signal. NM01 began to cross the road in the direct path of V01. Subsequently, the front right of V01 collided with NM01. NM01 fell to the ground coming to final rest facing south in the intersection of US 19 and Toucan Trail. V01 relocated near the area of collision.

On [DATE] at approximately [TIME], I was dispatched to the intersection located at Collier Parkway/State Road 54, Lutz, FL, in reference to a motor vehicle crash in which had just occurred. Upon arrival, I made contact with HCSO deputies who were out with Driver 1 of Vehicle 1, [NAME], who was parked in the parking lot of the Suncoast Credit Union Bank located at [ADDRESS], Lutz, FL. HCSO deputies advised they had not witnessed the crash but had stopped at the crash to ensure all involved parties were okay. Fire rescue 23 had also been on scene and received refusals for all involved parties reference [CASE NUMBER]. I then began conducting the crash investigation. Driver 1 advised he had been travelling west bound on State Road 54, and had looked into the back of his vehicle to put his pillow in the back seat. Driver 1 stated as he looked forward again, he was struck on the driver's side of his vehicle by Vehicle 2. Driver 1 advised he was unsure if the light at the intersection had been green, but stated it was possible the light could have been red for his direction of travel. Driver 1 also advised it was possible he was travelling on the wrong side of the road, going west bound in the east bound lanes of travel. Driver 1 believed he was going the speed limit and with the flow of traffic as well. Driver 1 stated he then pulled into the parking lot and waited for the arrival of law enforcement. I then made contact with Driver 2 of vehicle 2, who advised he had been travelling north bound on Collier Parkway, due to having a green light for his direction of travel, when his vehicle struck Vehicle 1. Driver 2 believed vehicle 1 had been travelling in the east bound lanes while travelling west bound on State Road 54. Driver 2 did not see vehicle 1 until they had collided. Vehicle 1 had major and disabling damage along the entire driver's side of the vehicle. Vehicle 1 appeared to have had been hit on the driver's side, with Vehicle 2's front bumper and continued driving causing damage down the entire side. Vehicle 2 sustained major and disabling damage on the front end of the vehicle consistent with it colliding into the diver's side of Vehicle 1. Both vehicles were able to get off of the road way.

Vehicle 1 was traveling west in the center lane of State Road 54 approaching Collier Pkwy. Vehicle 2 was traveling south in the inside lane of Collier Pkwy approaching State Road 54. Driver 1 failed to stop at the steady red traffic signal and proceeded through the intersection while occupied by Vehicle 2. The right side of Vehicle 1's trailer struck the front of Vehicle 2 within the roadway. Upon Trooper's arrival, both vehicles had been relocated from area of collision to the north shoulder of State Road 54. Driver 1 was cited for violation of a steady red traffic signal.

Vehicle 1 (V1) was northbound on US Highway 19, just north of Flora Avenue. Non-Motorist 1 (NM1) was crossing the northbound lanes of US Highway 19 eastbound. The driver of V1 stated that she felt something crawl on her which caused her to lose control of the vehicle and swerve. The left front struck NM1. V1 was removed from the roadway prior to my arrival. NM1 was transported to Bayonet Point Medical Center prior to me arriving on scene.

Vehicle 1 was traveling south in the inside lane of U.S. Highway 19 approaching Sunray Drive. Vehicle 2 was traveling west in the left turn lane of Sunray Drive approaching U.S. Highway 19. Driver 1 failed to stop at the steady red light. As a result, the front left of Vehicle 1 struck the right side of Vehicle 2. Vehicle 1 came to final rest at the southwest corner of the intersection, facing west. Vehicle 2 came to final rest across the inside and center southbound lanes, facing south. Upon Trooper's arrival, both vehicles remained at final rest.

V01 was traveling southbound on US Highway 19 (State Road 55) in the inside left turn lane approaching a red left turn traffic signal at State Road 52. V02 was traveling northbound on US Highway 19 (State Road 55) in the inside lane approaching a green traffic signal at State Road 52. Driver-1 failed to stop at a red traffic signal and attempted to make a left turn onto State Road 52 east. As a result, V01 traveled into the path of V02 and the front left of V02 struck the right front of V01. V01 came to final rest in the area of colision of US Highway 19 and State Road 52 facing south. V02 rotated clockwise and traveled east into the westbound lanes of State Road 52 and came to final rest in the right turn lane east of US Highway 19 facing southeast. Contributing cause- Driver-1 failed to stop at a red traffic signal causing a collision with V02. Trooper watched video footage and was able to observe the traffic pattern and that north and south lanes were traveling at the time of the collision indicating that V01 had a red left turn traffic signal at the time of the collision.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was traveling southbound on U.S. 19 (State Road 55), in the outside lane, just north of State Road 52. Vehicle 2 (V02) was stopped, southbound on U.S. 19 (State Road 55), in the outside lane, just north of State Road 52, directly ahead of V01. Based upon the physical evidence to V01 and V02, as well as the damage to the roadway, it appears as if the right front of V01 collided with the rear of V02. Driver 2 was ejected from V02, and propelled into the air. Driver 2's body then collided with the roadway. V02 overturned onto its right side, and came to final rest in the southbound right turn lane, south of the intersection. V01 was relocated to the southbound grass shoulder of U.S. 19, south of the intersection, prior to my arrival.

V01 was traveling southbound in the outside lane on U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55), approaching Sunray Drive. V02 and trailer of V02 were traveling eastbound in the left turn lane on Sunray Drive, approaching U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55). There are traffic control signal lights at the intersection of U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55) and Sunray Drive. The traffic control signal light was a solid red circle for north and southbound traffic on U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55). The traffic control signal light was a green left turn arrow for eastbound traffic on Sunray Drive. V02 and trailer of V02 began proceeding into the intersection to make a left turn onto U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55), As V02 and trailer of V02 entered the intersection, V01 failed to stop and proceeded into the intersection. The front of V01 struck the left side of V02. V01, V02, and trailer of V02 were relocated from the area of collision to the Aldi's parking lot located at [ADDRESS], prior to my arrival. Upon my arrival, V01, V02, and trailer of V02 remained where they were relocated to.

Vehicle 1 was traveling north in the outside lane of US Highway 19(State Road 55), approaching Citrus Drive with a red light traffic control device. Vehicle 2 was traveling west on Citrus Drive to make a left turn and go south on US Highway 19(State Road 55) with a green light traffic control device. The driver of Vehicle 1 failed to stop at the red light. When Driver 1 saw Vehicle 2, attempted to avoid the collision by steering to the right, however, driver 1 was unable to avoid the collision. As a result, the front left corner of Vehicle 1 collided with the left side of Vehicle 2. Both vehicles were relocated to the westbound lanes of Citrus Drive prior to my arrival.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was traveling south on US 19 (State Road 55) approaching Fox Hollow Drive in the left turn lane. Vehicle 2 (V02) was traveling north on US 19 (State Road 55) approaching Fox Hollow Drive in the inside lane. Vehicle (V03) was traveling north on US 19 (State Road 55) approaching Fox Hollow Drive in center lane. Driver 2 and Driver 3 approached the intersection and stopped their vehicles respective at the stop bar for a red signal without incident. The traffic signal for northbound US 19 (State Road 55) changed from red to green and Driver 2 and Driver 3 proceeded north into the intersection. Driver 1 stopped V01 at the stop bar for a red left arrow without incident. Driver 1 observed that the southbound signal for US 19 (State Road 55) turned from red to green, and believing her signal changed, initiated a left turn into the intersection through the red left signal. As a result, the passenger's side front corner of V02 collided with the passenger's side of V01. V01 began to rotate in a clockwise direction resulting in the passenger's side front corner bumper of V03 collided with the passenger's side rear corner of V01. V01, V02 and V03 were all moved from final rest prior to my arrival.

Vehicle 1 was traveling east in the parking lot address of [ADDRESS] approaching a stop sign, west of Collier Pkwy. Vehicle 2 was traveling north on Collier Pkwy in the outside lane, north of State Road 54. Vehicle 1 turned left (northeast) from the stop sign as Vehicle 2 was approaching. The front of Vehicle 1 struck the left side of Vehicle 2. Vehicle 1 and 2 relocated off the roadway prior to my arrival.

Pre Crash: V01 (Vehicle 1) was traveling east in the left turn lane of SR 60 (E Brandon Blvd) approaching the intersection with Parsons Ave S. V02 (Vehicle 2) was traveling north in the right lane of Parsons Ave S, approaching the intersection with SR 60 (E Brandon Blvd). Crash: V01 executed a left turn from SR 60 to travel north on Parsons Ave S. At the same time, V02 traveled north through the intersection to continue north on Parsons Ave S. This caused the front of V01 to collide with the front left of V02. Post Crash: Both vehicles came to controlled stops in a parking lot located at the southeast corner of the intersection. Statements: According to Driver 1, she had a solid green light to continue into the intersection. According to Driver 2, she had a solid green light to continue into the intersection. Observations: No tire marks or debris were observed when conducting this traffic crash investigation. No video of the intersection were located. No citations were issued due to conflicting statements.

V01 was traveling northbound in the center lane of US Highway 19 approaching the intersection of Sunray Drive. V02 was stopped in traffic at a steady red arrow in the westbound left turn lane of Sunray Drive intersecting with US Highway 19 (State Road 55). Based on statements from Driver-2, the red arrow turned green to proceed across the intersection and make a left turn on to the southbound lane of US Highway 19. Driver-2 stated that she was the second care in line and the first care had proceeded forward and she followed. As V02 entered the intersection V01 was also occupying the intersection. The front right of V01 collided with the front left side of V02. V02 was turned almost 360 degree clock wise in the intersection till it came to final rest in the northbound lanes facing south. Driver-1 stated that she was traveling northbound in the center lane of US Highway 19 approaching the intersection of Sunray Drive. Driver-1 stated that she had a solid green light to proceed through the intersection. As she entered the intersection she observed V02 crossing the intersection and attempted to change lanes in to the northbound inside lane to avoid a collision but was unable to do so. After the collision V01 cross the southbound lanes of traffic and came to final rest on the westbound lanes of Sunray Drive on the west side of the intersection. At the time of this Trooper's arrival V02 was still at final rest in the roadway and Driver-2 and passenger had been transported to the hospital. V01 and been moved off the roadway and on to the grass shoulder of the westbound lanes of Sunray Drive west of the intersection. Trooper was given Witness information and was able to make contract. Witness stated that she was in the eastbound left turn lane to turn on to the northbound lanes of traffic on US Highway 19. She was stopped at a steady red arrow. The arrow turned green and she seen traffic across from her begin to proceed. Then she seen the collision. Trooper observed the traffic patterned from the point of view of the witness and observed that at the time the turn arrow goes green both north and south turning traffic while turn at the same time, and the traffic traveling north and south on US Highway 19 will stop for solid reds. Based on statements and observations it is believed that Driver-1 failed to stop at a red light and caused a collision.

V1 traveled west on a private driveway near ([ADDRESS]). V1 exited the parking lot and began making a left turn to travel south on Parsons Ave. Meanwhile, V2 was traveling north on Parsons Ave in the left lane. The front driver side of V2 struck the driver side doors of V1. The impact turned V1 counter clockwise. V1 then made rear to front contact with V3, which had come to a stop in the southbound left turn lane. V1 sustained functional damage and was moved to the nearby parking lot. The vehicle was locked although a rear driver side window was broken. The owner requested I not contact a tow company and they would have the vehicle towed upon their own accord. V2 sustained functional damage although the front air bag was deployed. The owner elected to have it towed via his insurance company. V3 sustained minimal damage and was driven from the scene. D1 and their passenger (V1's R/O) were both transported to Brandon Regional by AMR [ID] ([ID]). I later learned they both were experiencing general pain. D2 sustained an abrasion to their hand and D3 reported no injuries. D1 stated there was an opening so she began to turn. She was not going fast. She then remembers being hit. The car must have been going fast. D2 advised he was in the left lane. V1 then began turning in front of him very slowly. He hit his brakes but could not stop. D3 advised she was approaching the intersection to turn. V1 pulled out in front of V2 and they hit, then hit her. V3 was equipped with a dash camera. The footage was provided to me and impounded as evidence. The footage clearly shows V1 pull onto Parsons Ave. and begin turning at a slow speed. The contact between V1 and V2 occurs before V1 collides with V3. Digital photographs were taken and uploaded into Evidence.com.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was traveling west on SR 50 (Cortez Blvd) in the left turn lane approaching Weeping Willow St. Vehicle 2 (V02) was traveling east on SR 50 (Cortez Blvd) in the right turn lane approaching Mariner Blvd. Vehicle 3 (V03) was traveling east on SR 50 (Cortez Blvd) in the outside lane approaching Mariner Blvd. While Vehicle 1 (V01) was traveling on SR 50, Driver 1 (D01) attempted to negotiate a left hand turn across eastbound traffic. V01 was traveling west on SR-54 in the left turn lane approaching the intersection of Collier Parkway. V02 was stopped eastbound on SR-54 in the middle lane for the red traffic signal at the intersection of Collier Parkway. The traffic signal for eastbound traffic on SR-54 turned green, subsequently, V02 began to travel eastbound onto the intersection of Collier Parkway. V01 proceeded to make a left turn (south) from the westbound left turn lane of SR-54 into the intersection of Collier Parkway and into the direct path of V02, failing to yield the right of way to V02. As a result, the front right corner of V01 collided with the front right corner of V02. Post collision, V02 traveled across the intersection of Collier Parkway and pulled onto the outside grass shoulder of SR-54. V01 continued south on Collier Parkway without stopping to assess damage or make contact with the driver of V02. V01 was described a s a black in color pickup truck, no other information for either the vehicle nor the driver were obtained.

V01 was traveling east in the straight lane of SR-52, west of US-19 (SR-55). V02 was traveling south in the outside lane of US-19, approaching SR-52. V01 proceeded straight ahead to travel across US-19. V01 entered the outside lane into the path of V02. As a result, the front left of V01 collided with the right side of V02. Post collision, V01 came to final in the southwest corner of the intersection. V02 came to final rest in the south outside lane of US-19. The witness was stopped at the red left turn signal on westbound SR-52, at the intersection of US-19. The witness stated V01 proceed straight ahead into the intersection while V02 traveled south through the intersection. The witness stated north and southbound US-19 had green traffic signals. Driver-1 stated she had a green traffic signal to travel straight on SR-52. Driver-2 stated he was unsure of the traffic signal for V02 at the time of collision. Driver-2 stated he was trying to fold his sun visor down as he could not see due to the sun. Therefore, it is undetermined which vehicle is at-fault due to the uncertainty of the traffic signals for each respective vehicle.

V01 was traveling southbound in the Crunch Fitness driveway exit/ entrance located at [ADDRESS], approaching the west travel lanes of State Road 54 and was just east of Collier Parkway. The vision of Driver-1 was obstructed by the stopped traffic as he steered V01 in a southwest direction into the inside lane of State Road 54, which was occupied by V02. As a result the front and left side of V01 struck the right side of V02. V01 and V02 were moved from the area of collision to the grass median of State Road 54, prior to Trooper's arrival. V01 and V02 were facing west in the median, and both were still fully functional. All occupants refused to be transported by Pasco County EMS while on scene.

V01 was traveling south on Collier Parkway, south of State Road 54. V02 was traveling north in the right turn lane of Collier Parkway, approaching State Road 54. V01 proceeded to make a left turn to enter the Willow Bend Towne Centre parking lot. V01 subsequently traveled into the path of V02. As a result, the right side of V01 collided with the front of V02. Post collision, V01 came to final rest facing north in the right turn lane of northbound Collier Parkway. V02 came to final rest facing north in the parking lot entrance way. Both vehicles remained at final rest upon my arrival.

V01 was traveling southbound in the left turn lane on U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55), south of State Road 52. V02 was traveling northbound in the continuous right turn lane on U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55), south of State Road 52. Traffic traveling on the northbound inside, center and outside lanes of U.S. Highway 19 (SR-55) came to a stop. V01 then proceeded to turn left. Driver 1 failed to observe V02 approaching in the continous right turn lane and came into the direct path of V02. Driver 1 violated the right of way of V02. The front left corner of V02 struck the right side of V01. Both vehicles were relocated from the area of collision to the La Vista Inn located at [ADDRESS], prior to my arrival. Upon my arrival, both vehicles remained where they relocated to.

V1 was exiting a private driveway, attempting to make a left turn onto Parsons Ave, to head southbound, approximately 500ft south of Brandon Blvd. V2 was stopped in traffic in northbound traffic on Parsons Ave at the same location as V1. V2 came to a stop and waved V1 to pull out onto the roadway. V1 began making the left turn, and the front driver bumper of V1 and the front driver bumper of V2 struck one another. The driver of V1 advised that the driver of V2 had waved her on and then V2 had struck her. There was no evidence that V2 intentionally struck V1. The driver of V1 was advised she would be at fault for the crash. Neither vehicle required a tow truck, and there were no complaints of injury.

Vehicle one (V01) was traveling eastbound on SR-60 (Brandon Blvd) in the left turn lane approaching a private road to Walmart just west of Mt Carmel Rd. Vehicle two (V02) was traveling westbound on SR-60 (Brandon Blvd) in the right lane approaching Mt Carmel Rd. V01 proceeded to turn left, northbound, to a private road. The front portion of V02 collided into the front right portion of V01. Both vehicles came to final rest at the point of impact and were moved onto the right shoulder of SR-60 west prior to my arrival. No skid marks were noted at this scene.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was traveling south on US 19 (SR 55) in the outside center lane approaching Innisbrook Dr. Vehicle 2 (V02) was traveling east on Innisbrook Dr approaching US 19 (SR 55). Vehicle 3 (V03) was traveling north on US 19 (SR 55) in the inside lane approaching Innisbrook Dr. While Vehicle 1 (V01) was traveling on US 19, Driver 1 (D01) failed to stop for a red traffic control light, entering into the intersection. Vehicle 1 (V01) was stopped at the red light in the inside southbound lane on US 19. Vehicle 2 (V02) was turning left from the northbound lane of US 19 on a green arrow. V02 came to final rest facing northwest in the intersection blocking the right two southbound lanes of US 19.

Vehicle 1 (V01) was northbound on Parsons ave in the outside lane continuing through the intersection. Vehicle 2 (V02) was eastbound on SR-60 continuing through the intersection. Vehicle-1 was traveling north on CR 587 (Mariner Blvd) in the inside left turn lane. Vehicle-2 was traveling east on SR 50 (Cortez Blvd) in the U-turn lane and was stopped for a red signal. Vehicle 1 (V01) was stopped southbound on an access road east of St. Cloud Avenue on the north side of State Road 60. V01 was stopped at a stop sign. V01 was traveling north in the inside left turn lane on County Road 587, approaching State Road 50. V02 was stopped in the u-turn lane on State Road 50 facing east, just west of County Road 587. Vehicle 1 was traveling south in the left turn lane of Collier Parkway, south of State Road 54. Vehicle 2 was traveling north in the outside lane of Collier Parkway approaching State Road 54. This case was originally assigned to Trooper [NAME] on [DATE] at [TIME] Due to Trooper [NAME] resignation, I, Trooper [NAME] have taken over as the lead investigator in this crash. On [DATE] at approximately [TIME] I was traveling northbound on E Parsons Ave when I was waved down by D2 for a traffic crash that was voiced out as an alert as a hit and run by dispatch. I pulled over and conducted an interview with D2 (see interview). It was learned V2 was driving straight on the intersection of E Parsons Ave and E Brandon Blvd when V1 who was turning left from Northbound E Parsons Ave crashed into V2. D2 stated she had a green light and V1 did not have a green turn arrow. D1 stated that D2 pulled over on the parking lot of [ADDRESS], Brandon, FL [ADDRESS] and attempted to exchange information, but a disagreement occurred and D2 drove off. I was able to obtain a [PLATE] of V1 from D2 and was able to contact D2. I then contacted a phone interview with D2 but was not able to meet with D2 due to call volume. D1 stated they were turning left onto westbound E Brandon Blvd and did not have a green turn arrow and was only on a solid green light, confirming that V2 had the right of way. D1 sent a picture confirming she did attempt to report the crash to law enforcement and only left after obtaining insurance contact from D1.V2 was hit on the left front of the vehicle and suffered an estimated $1500 worth of damage due to possible frame damage. V1 was hit on the front right and suffered an estimated $1000 of damage through pictures sent by D1. I was able to send D1 and D2 a drivers exchange form for drivers exchange and concluded that there was no hit and run that occurred reference this crash. D1 stated the following: She was driving south on Parsons Ave when V1 crashed into her left side. She pulled into the parking lot of Brandon Signs and attempted to exchange information, but a disagreement occurred when D1 stated "don't mess with me" and left. D1 called her mother to meet at the location and was calling 911 when I was flagged down at the intersection. D1 stated she was driving 30 mph on the middle lane and had a green arrow at the time of the collision. D2 did not have a green arrow. D2 stated the following: She was driving on the left turn lane northbound on Parsons Ave at the intersection when she attempted to make the left turn, V2 crashed into her. D2 was going fast and was on the phone, possibly not paying attention. D1 did not know if D2 was turning or going straight. D1 and D2 pulled into the Brandon Signs Parking lot and attempted to exchange information. D2's boyfriend was on the phone and was trying to offer to pay cash for the damage instead of going through insurance. D1 only left after getting the policy number of D2 and thought they both had enough of information.

Through my investigation, I determined V1 was turning left from westbound Brandon Blvd E onto an access way and V2 was traveling east on Brandon Blvd E prior to this incident. V1 failed to yield the right of way and entered into the path of V2 while trying to complete this left turn. This action resulted in the front of V2 colliding with the right side of V1. This collision caused both vehicles to come to final rest on the access road on the east side of HGreg, located at [ADDRESS] E. Before coming to final rest, V1 collided with two small posts on the property of HGreg. HCFR responded to the scene however none of the involved parties were transported to the hospital while on scene. Disabling damage was observed to both vehicles. D1 advised she had just left Chick Fil A on the north side of Brandon Blvd E and got into the left turn lane. She was going to cross Brandon Blvd E and cut through a nearby parking lot. Prior to making the left turn, she observed V2 traveling east on Brandon Blvd E. She thought she would be able to make the turn so she proceeded across the roadway. It appeared to her that V2 accelerated prior to this collision, after she started to complete the turn. As she was crossing Brandon Blvd E the collision occurred. D2 advised he was traveling east on Brandon Blvd E prior to this collision. As he was approaching the incident location he was traveling approximately 50mph. V1 made a left turn in front of him. He tried to avoid the collision but was unsuccessful. The witness listed on this report advised she was traveling north on the access road on the east side of HGreg prior to this incident. She observed V1 making a left turn to cross Brandon Blvd E, and turn into the path of V2. East Lake Towing responded to the scene and removed both vehicles. I responded to HGreg and made contact with management who advised they had video footage of this incident. I reviewed this footage which shows v1 making a left turn into the path of V2. The collision occurred and both vehicles end up on the access road on the east side of HGreg. I had no further involvement in this incident.

V1 was traveling westbound in the left turn lane on Flora Ave at US Highway 19. V2 was traveling eastbound in the straight and right turn lane on Flora Ave at US Highway 19. The driver of V1 turned left into the path of V2. As a result, the right side of V1 collided with the front right of V2. Both vehicles moved from the area of collision to the Wells Fargo bank parking lot at [ADDRESS] prior to my arrival. The driver of V1 stated that his traffic signal had a steady green light with a steady green left turn arrow, that changed to yellow then turned off, leaving only the solid green signal. He stated he was already within the intersection when he observed the yellow arrow turn off. He stated he believed it was clear to turn left. The driver of V2 stated her traffic signal was steady green the entire time she approached the intersection while traveling. She stated there were other cars ahead of her that proceeded straight (eastbound) across US Highway 19. She stated V1 approached from the opposite direction and suddenly turned in front of her. She stated there was nothing she could do to avoid the collision. I observed the traffic signal pattern for the 4-way intersection. The first phase allows the northbound and southbound left turn lanes of US Highway 19 turn left. After those change to steady red, the next phase allow northbound and southbound straight lanes of US Highway 19 change to steady green. After those change to red, the next phase allows all westbound traffic on Flora Ave proceed straight and turn left with a solid green and green left turn arrow. The next phase, the westbound left turn arrow changes to yellow and turns off while the straight signal remains solid green. The next phase, westbound and eastbound straight signals are green to allow straight traffic to proceed on Flora Ave, requiring drivers the yield while making a left turn. Based on my observations of the traffic control signal, it is probable that the driver of V1 failed to yield to V2 while making a left turn. No citation was issued due to no additional witnesses and lack of evidence that are able to prove a case in court beyond a reasonable doubt.

Vehicle 1 was eastbound in the continuous left turn lane on SR-54 at the intersection with Village Oaks Plaza Dr. Vehicle 2 was westbound on in the middle lane on SR-54 approaching the intersection with Village Oaks Plaza Dr. Driver 1 stated that he entered into the middle of the intersection observing a flashing yellow left turn arrow in anticipation of initiating a left turn onto Village Lakes Plaza Dr. Driver 1 stated that he observed the vehicles in the westbound inside and outside lanes come to a stop then initiated a left turn. As the vehicle was overturned back upright the rear of Vehicle 2 struck and knocked down the pole.

On [DATE] at approximately [TIME] I responded to the Circle K gas station located at [ADDRESS], Spring Hill in reference to an agency vehicle crash. Upon arrival contact was made with W1 who stated he believed to have seen V1 Deputy patrol car to be heading northbound and V2 to be heading southbound on Commercial way. W1 stated both vehicles meet at the intersection and due to the incident happening so quickly he could not tell me who struck who. Evidence at the scene and video evidence proved the statement by W1 was incorrect. Contact was made with V2 driver who stated he was heading northbound on Commercial Way when suddenly a vehicle turned left in front of him causing him to crash into the car's rear tire. V2 driver stated the incident occurred so fast he did not notice V1 was a Deputy patrol car. V2 driver did not report any injuries at the scene. Contact was made with V3 driver who stated he was sitting at the red light at the intersection of Toucan Trail and Commercial Way when suddenly a crash occurred in front of him which caused debris to struck his front bumper. V3 driver reported no injuries. V1 driver was transported to Tampa General Hospital Spring Hill. Contact was made with V1 driver at the Hospital later and he advised the incident occurred so fast he only remembers having the yellow arrow to turn left at the intersection of Commercial Way and Toucan trail southbound lane and him also having a call for service at the Circle K for an alleged physical disturbance. V1 driver stated he then remembers trying to turn in front of a car to get to the call for service faster and thats it. V1 driver was seen by medical professional in regards to possible injuries to the crash. I then made contact with the Circle K representative who was able to show me video of the crash. In the video the traffic light is not visible due to being blocked by the roof of the gas pumps. In the video I was able to observed as V1 was stopped at the left turn lane at the intersection Commercial Way and Toucan Trail southbound lane. I then observed as V1 attempted the left turn by turning in front of V2 not allowing him enough time to react causing the crash. The video will later be admitted into evidence. V1 driver was cited accordingly
